**Instructions.** Complete this assignment in Quarto or R Markdown and upload
both your `.qmd` source and the rendered `.html` to Brightspace. Show your code. Interpretation questions are
graded on precision (adjusted for what, units, association vs causation,
population), exactly as practiced in the labs. End with your AI-use statement
(see Section 4).

**Data.** A British survey of 47 teenagers on gambling and its covariates:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data(teengamb, package = "faraway")
```

Variables used below: `gamble` = expenditure on gambling (pounds per year),
`income` = income (pounds per week), `sex` = 0 for male, 1 for female,
`status` = socioeconomic status score of parents. Note that `sex` is coded
numerically; you may use it as is or convert it to a labeled factor.

# Section 1: Do (6 points)

**1.1** Fit the multiple regression of `gamble` on `income`, `sex`, and
`status`. Report the coefficient table and R-squared. (2 pts)

**1.2** For two profiles, (a) a male with `income` 5 and `status` 50, and
(b) a female with `income` 5 and `status` 50, compute both the 95% confidence
interval for the mean response and the 95% prediction interval for a new
individual, using `predict()` with `interval = "confidence"` and
`interval = "prediction"`. Present the four intervals in a small table. (2 pts)

**1.3** Make the residuals-versus-fitted plot for your model (residuals on
the y axis, fitted values on the x axis, with a horizontal line at zero).
(2 pts)

# Section 2: Interpret (8 points; interpretation precision counts double)

**2.1** Using the male profile from 1.2, explain in two sentences, in plain
words a public health colleague could follow, what the confidence interval
estimates and what the prediction interval estimates, and why the prediction
interval is so much wider. (2 pts)

**2.2** Describe what you see in the residual plot from 1.3. Name the
specific assumption violations the plot shows (there are at least two:
consider the spread of the residuals across fitted values, and their
symmetry), and point to the features of the plot that reveal them. (2 pts)

**2.3** Given your diagnosis in 2.2, would you trust the 95% prediction
intervals from 1.2 to actually cover new observations 95% of the time?
Explain in two sentences which specific violation undermines the PI and how
(think about what the PI formula assumes about the error distribution).
(2 pts)

**2.4** Propose a remedy: refit the model with `sqrt(gamble)` as the outcome
(or `log(gamble + 1)` if you prefer), remake the residual plot, and state in
two sentences whether the problems improved and what interpretability price
you paid for the fix. (2 pts)

# Section 3: Critique the AI (6 points)

A student gave this dataset to an AI assistant and asked for a prediction
write-up. The assistant replied:

> "The model `gamble ~ income + sex + status` explains 61% of the variation
> in gambling expenditure. For a male teenager with income 5 and status 50,
> the 95% confidence interval is (21.4, 39.0) pounds, so we can be 95% sure
> that this individual will spend between 21 and 39 pounds per year on
> gambling. Since the model fits well, the regression assumptions are clearly
> satisfied and residual plots are unnecessary. The model is also useful well
> beyond the survey: a teenager earning 20 pounds per week is predicted to
> spend 104 pounds per year, an especially reliable prediction because it
> comes directly from the fitted equation. Finally, for a female with income
> 1 and status 60 the model predicts -15.4 pounds, meaning she would earn
> about 15 pounds per year from gambling."

**3.1** This paragraph contains at least four distinct statistical errors.
Identify each one you find (quote the offending phrase), and explain in one
or two sentences why it is wrong. Finding four earns full credit; a fifth
earns a bonus point. (4 pts + 1 bonus)

**3.2** Verify the AI's numbers: compute the model's R-squared and the
predicted `gamble` for a male with income 20 and status 50 yourself. Report
which of the AI's numbers match and which do not, and write one sentence on
why the income-20 prediction should not be trusted even where the arithmetic
is right. (2 pts)

# Section 4: AI-use statement (required, ungraded)

One or two sentences: which AI tools you used on this assignment and for what,
or "No AI tools used." Note that Section 3 asks you to critique provided AI
output; using an AI to critique the AI is permitted, but the errors you report
